q:
There are three taps of diameter 1 cm, 4/3 cm and 2 cm, respectively. 
The ratio of the water flowing through them is equal to the ratio of the square of their diameters. 
The biggest tap can fill the tank alone in 61 min. 
If all the taps are opened simultaneously, how long will the tank take to be filled?
e:
Time taken to fill the tank by the tap having 2 cm diameter = 61 min

∴ Time taken to fill the tank by the tap having 1 cm diameter 
= 61 x (2/1)2 = 244 min

Similarly, time taken to fill the tank by the tap having 4/3 cm diameter
= 61 x [(2 x 3)/4]2 = 61 x 9/4 = 549/4 min.

∴ Part of the tank filled by all the three pipes in 1 min
= 1/61 + 1/244 + 1/(549/4)
= (36 + 9 + 16)/2196 = 61/2196 = 1/36
Hence, required time taken = 36 min

q:
Two pipes A and B can fill a tank in 20 and 30 minutes respectively.
If both the pipes are used together,then how long will it take to fill the tank ?
e:
Part filled by A in 1 min = 1/20 ,  part filled by B in 1 min = 1/30
Part filled by (A + B) in 1 min = 1/20 + 1/30 = 1/12
hence  Both the pipes can fill the tank in 12  minutes.

q:
A leak in the lower portion of a tank can empty the full tank in 9 hrs. 
An inlet pipe fills water at the rtae of 10 lit. a minute.  
When the tank is full, the inlet is opened and due to leak, the tank is empty in 16 hrs.  
How many litres does the cistern hold ?
e:
Work done by the inlet in 1 hr = 

1/9−1/16=7/144

Work done by the inlet in 1 min. = (7/144 × 1/60)=7/8,640

Volume of  7/8,640 part = 10 litres.

Whole volume = 
10×8,640/7=12,342 litres.

q:
Pipes A, B and C which fill the tank together in 6 hours are opened for 2 hours after which pipe C was closed. 
Find the number of hours taken by pipe C to fill the tank if the remaining tank is filled in 7 hours.
e:
1/A + 1/B + 1/C = 1/6
Now given that first all open for 2 hours, then C closed and A+B completes in 7 hours, so
(1/A + 1/B + 1/C) *2 + (1/A + 1/B)*7 = 1
Put 1/A + 1/B = 1/6 – 1/C
(1/6 – 1/C + 1/C) *2 + (1/6 – 1/C)*7 = 1
2/6 + 7/6 – 7/C = 1
Solve, C = 14

A tank can be filled by two tap A and B in 8 hour and 10 hours respectively. 
The full tank can be emptied by the third tap in 9 hours.

e:

Therefore, tap A fills 1/8 th part of the tank in 1 hour.
Tap B fills 1/10 th part of the tank in 1 hour.
Tap C empties out 1/9 th part of the tank in 1 hour.
Thus, in 1 hour (1/8 + 1/10 – 1/9) part of the tank is filled.
(45 + 36 – 40)/360 = 41/360 th part of the tank is filled.
Thus, tank will be filled completely in 360/41 hours, when all the three taps A, B and C are opened together.

q:
If two pipes function simultaneously, the reservoir will be filled in 12 hours. 
One pipe fills the reservoir 10 hours faster than the other. 
How many hours does the faster pipe take to fill the reservoir ?
e:
Suppose that one pipe takes N hours to fill the reservoir. Then another pipe takes (N - 10) hours.
∴ 1/N + 1/(N - 10) = 1/12
⇒ 12(N - 10 + N) = N(N - 10)
or N2 - 34N + 120 = 0
or (N - 30)(N - 4) = 0
∴ N = 30 or N = 4
So, the faster pipe takes 30 hours to fill the reservoir

q:

If both the taps are opened simultaneously,then after how much time will the cistern get filled ?
e:
Net part filled in 1 hour  = 1/4 - 1/9 = 5/36
∴ The cistern will be  filled  in 36/5 hrs i.e., 7.2 hrs.

q:
Three pipes A, B and C can fill a tank from empty to full in 30 minutes, 20 minutes and 10 minutes respectively. 
When the tank is empty, all the three pipes are opened. A, B and C discharge chemical solutions P, Q and R respectively. 
What is the proportion of solution R in the liquid in the tank after 3 minutes ?
e:
Part filled by (A + B + C) in 3 minutes = 3(1/30 + 1/20 + 1/10 ) = (3* (11/60)) = 11/20

Part filled by C in 3 minutes = 3/10

Required ratio = 3/10 * 20/11 = 6/11

After this, the tank will be completely filled in ?
e:
Part filled in 10 min.
= 10(1/20 + 1/60) = (10×(4/60)) = 2/3

Part filled by second tap in 1 min.= 1/60

1/60 : 1/3 :: 1:x ⇒ x = ((1/3)×1×60)=20 min.

e:

q:
A pipe can fill the tank in 5 hours.  Due to leakage at the bottom it is filled in 6 hours. 
When the tank is full, in how much time will it be empties by the leak?
e:
When there is no leakage, the pipe can fill the cistern in 5 hours.
Therefore, The pipe fills 1/5 th part of the tank in one hour.
When there is a leakage, the pipe can fill the cistern in 6 hours.
In case of leakage, the pipe fills 1/6 th part of the tank in one hour.
So, in 1 hour due to leakage (1/5 – 1/6) th 
                                    = (6 – 5)/30 th 
                                    = 1/30 th
The part of the tank is emptied. 
So, the tank will be emptied by leakage in 30 hours.

q:
If two pipes function together, the tank will be filled in 12 h . 
One pipe fills the tank in 10 h faster than the other. 
How many hours does the faster pipe take to fill up the tank?
e:
Let one pipe takes m h to fill the tank.
Then, the other pipe takes (m - 10) h.
According to the question.
∴ 1/m + 1/(m - 10) = 1/12
⇒ (m - 10 + m)/{m(m - 10)} = 1/12
⇒ 12m( m - 10 + m ) = ( m - 10 )
⇒ m^2 - 34m + 120 = 0 
⇒ m^2 - 30m - 4m + 120 = 0
⇒ ( m - 30 )( m - 4 ) = 0
∴ m = 30 or 4
∴ Faster pipe will take ( 30 - 10 ) h = 20 h to fill the tank.

q:
A tank can be filled by a tap in 20 min and by another tap in 60 min. Both the taps are kept open for 5 min and then the 1st tap is shut off.
After this, how much time the tank will be completely filled?
e:
Part of the tank filled by both taps in 5 min = 5 x (1/20 + 1/60) 
= 5 x (6 +2 )/120 = 8/24 = 1/3
∴ Remaining part = (1 - 1/3) = 2/3
∵ 1/60 Part is now filled in 1 min.
∴ 2/3 Part is now filled in 60 x 2/3 = 40 min.

There is a third pipe in the bottom of the cistern to empty it.

In how much time the third pipe alone can empty the cistern ?
e:

= 1/50 − (1/60 + 1/75 )=(1/50 − 3/100)=−1/100
. [- ve sign means emptying] 

The third pipe alone can empty the cistern in 100 min.

q:
A cistern has two taps which fill it in 12 min. and 15 min respectively .  
There is one outlet pipe in the cistern.  When all the taps & pipe are opened, the empty cistern is full in 20 min.  
How long will the waste pipe (outlet) take to empty the full cistern ?
e:
Work done by waste pipe in 1 minute

=1/20 − (1/12 + 1/15)= −1/10

Waste pipe will empty the full cistern in 10 minutes.

q: Three pipes, A, B and C are opened to fill a tank such that A and B cam fill the tank alone in 36 min. and 45 min. respectively and C can empty it in 30 min. After 6 minutes the emptying pipe is closed. In how many minutes the tank will be full in this way?
e:
Let the tank full in x minutes, then A and B opened for x minutes and C for 6 minutes.
(1/36 + 1/45)*x – (1/30)*6 = 1
(1/20)*x = 6/5
Solve, x = 24

q:
A and B are pipes such that A can empty the tank in 60 minutes and B can fill in 30 minutes.
The tank is full of water and pipe A is opened. 
If after 18 minutes, pipe B is also opened, then in how much total time the tank will be full again?
e:
Emptying pipe A is opened first for 18 minutes, so in 18 minutes the part of tank it has emptied is (1/60)*18 = 9/30
Now filling pipe is also opened, now since only 9/30 of the tank is empty so 9/30 is only to be filled by both pipes, let it take now x minutes, so
(1/30 – 1/60)*x = 9/30
Solve, x= 18
So total = 18+18 = 36 minutes [total time is asked – 18 minutes when emptyimh pipe was only opened, 18 minutes when both were operating.]

q:
One pipe can fill a tank three times as fast as another pipe. 
If together the two pipes can fill tank in 36 min, then the slower pipe alone will be able to fill the tank in?
e:
Let the slower pipe alone fill the tank in x min.
Then, faster pipe will fill it in x/3 min.
1/x + 3/x = 1/36
4/x = 1/36 => x = 144 min.

q:
Pipe A can fill a tank in 5 hours, pipe B in 10 hours and pipe C in 30 hours.
If all the pipes are open, in how many hours will the tank be filled?
e:
Part filled by A + B + C in 1 hour = 1/5 + 1/10 + 1/30 = 1/3
All the three pipes together will fill the tank in 3 hours.
